title: [Linux][IL2CPP] Player crashes loading embedded MonoScript with a null SerializeReference field
description:
A Linux IL2CPP player traps while loading its first scene when a programmatically added MonoBehaviour is saved with an embedded MonoScript and has one unread, null [SerializeReference] object field. The attached minimal project reproduces this on Unity 6000.5.6f1 (0e0577a1a2ac) and 6000.6.5f1 (3ff58d469c8a), with High managed stripping. Both builds report Succeeded, zero errors, and one missing/invalid-script warning; both players exit 133 before their managed startup marker.

The project deliberately retains invalid script registration: ProbePlayerHook.cs declares two MonoBehaviours, and only ProbePlayerHook matches the filename. ProbeHost was added using AddComponent<ProbeHost>() and saved in the supplied Assets/Probe.unity as an embedded MonoScript without a script asset GUID. We acknowledge Unity's filename/class mapping limitation and do not request support for this arrangement. This report concerns the resulting native player crash and build/error handling: the Editor permits creating/saving this component and a successful build, but the player cannot load the resulting scene.

Actual player log:
The file '.../Probe_Data/level0' is corrupted! Remove it and launch unity again!
[Position out of bounds!]
The expected MRP_SCENE_LOADED marker never appears. The Linux process exits 133 (SIGTRAP).

Expected behavior: reject the invalid component or fail the build with a clear diagnostic, or handle the invalid script reference during loading without a native trap.

Passing controls, tested on 6000.5.6f1: (1) the same runtime source under Mono loads and prints the startup marker; (2) moving ProbeHost into ProbeHost.cs and recreating the scene makes IL2CPP load successfully; (3) removing its sole field also makes IL2CPP load, even though the embedded MonoScript and missing-script warning remain. Some repeat builds in the same Editor session pass; fresh independent project copies without Library consistently reproduced the failing first build in our checks, so reproducibility is marked sometimes overall.

The runtime source is 22 lines. There is no third-party package, source generator, generic type, payload instance, or serialization callback. The 6.6 import kept both C# files and the saved scene byte-identical; Unity updated ProjectVersion and added com.unity.modules.tetgen 1.0.0 to the manifest. Both Linux SDK/toolchain dependencies stayed at 1.1.0. Tests ran under Xvfb with -batchmode -nographics. The 6.5 batch-mode Editor also exited 139 during shutdown after reporting a successful build; 6.6 built and exited 0. That shutdown behavior is separate from the player trap reported here.

Attachments include the small source project (no Library, binaries or builds), validation notes, build-result excerpts and player logs for both versions. This issue is separate from the previously reported 6.6 generic-struct serialization-callback Editor crash.
steps: Extract unity65-embedded-script-managed-reference-mrp.zip into a NEW directory, with no existing Library or build output. Use Linux x86_64 and Unity 6000.5.6f1 or 6000.6.5f1 with Linux IL2CPP support installed.

Open the extracted Unity65EmbeddedScriptManagedReference project. Accept the version upgrade if using 6000.6.5f1. Keep the supplied Assets/Probe.unity and ProbePlayerHook.cs unchanged; the incorrect registration is the trigger.

Select Tools > Unity 6.5 Repro > Build IL2CPP. Alternatively run Unity -batchmode -nographics -projectPath /absolute/project/path -executeMethod ProbeBuild.Build -logFile build.log. The builder selects StandaloneLinux64, IL2CPP, High stripping, Development, AllowDebugging and CleanBuildCache.
Observe a missing/invalid-script warning for ProbeHost, followed by MRP_BUILD=Succeeded;backend=IL2CPP and build-result.txt showing zero errors and one warning.
From the project directory run Builds/Probe/Probe.x86_64 -batchmode -nographics -logFile player.log. Observe level0 corruption / Position out of bounds, exit 133, and no MRP_SCENE_LOADED marker.

For the Mono control use another clean copy and Tools > Unity 6.5 Repro > Build Mono (or ProbeBuild.BuildMono), then launch the player: it prints MRP_SCENE_LOADED and exits 0 on 6000.5.6f1. Use separate clean copies for each comparison; warm repeated builds can differ.
